messages:
tess: Heads-up — seeing exporter flakiness to telemetry.vendor after the canary. gRPC requests dropping with `transport: connection lost` and TLS handshake errors. Anyone else?

nora: yep noticed ~10:30UTC, big spike in exporter latency + queue growth. looked like connections got reset under load. :warning:

ajay: which exporter (otelcol config)? grpc vs http? keepalive settings?

tess: gRPC (otlp). otelcol v0.83 sidecar. config snippet below — minimal, default send/queue options right now.

```yaml
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: telemetry.vendor.internal:4317
    tls:
      insecure: false
    headers:
      x-api-key: ${TELEMETRY_KEY}
    timeout: 8s
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 10ms
      max_interval: 5s
      max_elapsed_time: 30s
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      num_consumers: 2
      queue_size: 5000
```

nora: logs extracted:
```
2026-03-20T10:30:12Z exporter/otlp error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport: connection closed
2026-03-20T10:30:13Z exporter/otlp warn: TLS handshake timeout
2026-03-20T10:30:13Z exporter/sender debug: queue backlog=4600
```

ajay: two suspects: (1) gRPC connection churn / max concurrent streams on vendor side; (2) idle connection timeouts + keepalive mismatch causing vendor to drop. Also our retry backoff is too aggressive — small initial interval floods retries during a transient.

tess: makes sense. vendor said they close idle connections at 30s and also limit `max_concurrent_streams` to 100 per connection. we're doing a lot of short-lived connections.

ajay: propose quick patch: enable persistent keepalive pings, increase per-connection streams by using fewer dials (pool size), and tune backoff to exponential with larger initial interval. Example otelcol-ish overrides:

```yaml
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: telemetry.vendor.internal:4317
    tls:
      insecure: false
    timeout: 8s
    keepalive:
      time: 25s   # ping before vendor idle timeout
      timeout: 5s
    dial_options:
      grpc.max_concurrent_streams: 500
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 200ms
      max_interval: 10s
      max_elapsed_time: 120s
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      num_consumers: 6  # more workers, fewer dials
      queue_size: 10000
```

nora: good. also add a soft circuit-breaker: stop retries if exporter error rate > 20% for 1m, so we don't congest the vendor and our memory.

tess: +1. will open a tiny PR to update sidecar default and add a runtime flag to disable fallback to HTTP (we suspect HTTP/1.1 fallback increases connection churn).

ajay: also add tracing for exporter dial/conn lifecycle to our telemetry dashboard. need a per-exporter panel: active connections, streams, retry_rate, queue_depth, and TLS handshake errors. set alert: queue_depth > 5000 for 2m.

nora: quick repro I ran: forced vendor to close connections on idle and saw queue growth within 30s. test script attached (local):
```
# pseudo test
for i in $(seq 1 500); do 
  curl -X POST https://sidecar.local/emit -d '{"n":100}' &
done
sleep 40
kubectl logs -l app=otel-sidecar | grep exporter | tail -n 20
```

deploy-bot: deploy canary succeeded: services/telemetry-sidecar v2.13.1 -> v2.13.2 (10% traffic) :rocket:

tess: thanks — I'll push PR with keepalive + queue/workers + backoff defaults. also adding flag `telemetry.exporter.disable_http_fallback` to try removing fallback path for the canary.

ajay: on the roadmap item: follow-up to add runtime config so ops can tweak per-customer exporter pools and disable retries for noisy customers.

nora: action items: (1) tess PR to sidecar defaults, (2) ajay dashboard panels + alert, (3) ops runtime flag rollout. I'll monitor canary for 1h. :eyes:

tess: filing PR and RFC link: https://r.dev/repo/telemetry/exporter-conn-tuning

ajay: FYI — if vendor can't accept keepalive, fallback plan: shift to batching more aggressively and reduce export frequency for high-throughput jobs.

nora: noted. thanks all.

deploy-bot: alert cleared: exporter error_rate dropped below threshold at 10:52 UTC.
